scope: Four document-relative partial mappings: two exact Mind Code formulations against the 2022 Buschman/Miller review and 2023 Lundqvist et al. journal article. No claim of firstness over the target family, whole-program saturation, source dependence, or validation of SAN as a whole.

SAN.title: Mind Code // Brain Code: Go (Ancient Game) and Alpha Go
SAN.author: Micah Blumberg
SAN.date_boundary: Article metadata says published 30 June 2017 and modified 14 August 2018. The captured text is not individually backdated to either metadata date.
SAN.date_grade: A: archived public wording by capture date; earlier sentence-level date open

REVIEW.title: Working Memory Is Complex and Dynamic, Like Your Thoughts
REVIEW.date_boundary: Crossref records 1 December 2022; journal volume 35 issue 1 is 2023. DOI creation on 2 November 2022 is not a publication date. The 2021 SAN archive predates either 2022 date.

JOURNAL.title: Working memory control dynamics follow principles of spatial computing
JOURNAL.date_boundary: Received 16 March 2022; accepted 7 February 2023. The January 2021 preprint already contains the target family's spatial-gating proposal.

concepts.title: Thoughts have a pattern of activity and inhibition
concepts.quote: So that the shape of our thoughts, in tempo-spatial patterns is represented not only by what is excited in our brains but also by what is inhibited in our brains.
concepts.plain: SAN describes thought patterns using both active and inhibited regions. The later documents describe a changing spatial pattern that permits some memory-related activity and suppresses other activity.
concepts.residual: SAN's passage concerns the proposed spatial shape of thoughts. The target describes working-memory control with specified frequency bands and separates coarse control from fine-grained item coding. Those additional claims are not contained in this SAN sentence.

concepts.title: Selection changes what the network can express
concepts.quote: The inhibited parts of the brain should feature the unconscious material.
concepts.excerpt: the parts of you that are paying attention to something you are looking at become excited and that means they exhibit more activity
concepts.plain: SAN links attention to increased activity in selected regions and suppression elsewhere. The later accounts use inhibitory rhythms to regulate access to memory content.
concepts.residual: The shared operation is selective expression through excitation and inhibition. SAN's speculation about whole-brain electrical equilibrium and conscious/unconscious content is not established by the target experiments, and is not the target's stated explanation.

REVIEW-SHAPE.locator: PDF page 5 (printed page 21), Top–Down Control by Spatial Computing
REVIEW-SHAPE.quote: Control comes from where in network space a stimulus representation is currently expressed.
REVIEW-SHAPE.context: Pages 4–5 describe broad alpha/beta-versus-gamma patterns controlling the expression of finer-grained neural representations. Their location changes with task demands.

REVIEW-MASK.locator: PDF page 4 (printed page 20), control by oscillatory dynamics
REVIEW-MASK.quote: Alpha/beta inhibits gamma wherever they “collide” in cortex.
REVIEW-MASK.context: The surrounding paragraphs describe reduction of deep-layer alpha/beta allowing superficial recurrent excitation, gamma bursting and memory readout; increasing beta suppresses this activity.

JOURNAL-SHAPE.quote: The manifestation is a dynamic patchwork of beta and gamma bursts.
JOURNAL-SHAPE.context: The paragraph assigns control information to network space, distributing memory items across locations for independent manipulation, with beta inhibiting gamma/spiking where beta is high.

JOURNAL-MASK.quote: Beta bursts act as the control signal.
JOURNAL-MASK.context: The paragraph links beta to inhibition of gamma/spiking and thereby access to working-memory content. The next paragraphs explain how spatial control addresses individual items.

lens1.function: Both connect selective neural expression with the content that is currently available. This is a partial functional match, not equivalence of complete theories.
lens1.behavior: Both describe simultaneous higher activity in selected regions and inhibited activity elsewhere. The target adds specific task-dependent readout and control behavior.
lens1.operation: Spatially organized excitation/inhibition changes which neural content is expressed. The target assigns distinct roles to beta, gamma, spiking and item location; the SAN source does not specify that entire implementation.
lens1.math: No equation-to-equation equivalence is demonstrated in these passages. No formal numerical score or isomorphism proof is assigned.
lens1.program: An informal selection/gating subroutine can be translated between the descriptions. There is no executable implementation or verified program equivalence here.
lens1.form: A spatially and temporally differentiated neural pattern is shared; SAN thought-shape and target control-pattern are not treated as identical representational levels.

lens4.scope: One bounded Miller-coauthored program subset: January 2021 preprint, October 2022 revision identity and March 2023 journal in one version family, plus the distinct December 2022 Buschman/Miller review
lens4.finding: The spatial gating operation is present in the January 2021 preprint and persists in the reviewed 2022/2023 documents. The SAN article's preserved wording is earlier than the selected later documents. Direction of historical movement toward SAN is not resolved by these records.
lens4.before_control: Exact preprint P5–P8 retained as a chronology boundary, not a rival win or award.
lens4.open: October 2022 revision body and complete earlier/newest target history are not certified here. No program-level signature migration or genealogy verdict is asserted.
lens4.dependency_structure: Spatially differentiated excitation/inhibition is related to expression or availability of content. In SAN, the selection step is explicit in f236; d2a1 alone states a representational configuration.

stage_atom_matrix.finding: Excitation/inhibition shapes spatial activation maps for memory expression; full SAN thought/consciousness claim is not equated.
